o.w: Copying a snapshot into S3 and sharing an IAM user's long-term access keys exposes durable credentials to an external party, a much weaker and less secure sharing mechanism than scoped, encrypted cross-account snapshot and KMS key sharing.

explain:
Creating an encrypted snapshot ensures that the database data is protected during the transfer and storage process.
Sharing the encrypted snapshot with the auditor allows them to create their own copy of the database securely.
By allowing access to the AWS KMS encryption key, the auditor can decrypt the snapshot and restore it to their own environment.

q: A company stores data in PDF format in an Amazon S3 bucket. The company must follow a legal requirement to retain all new and existing data in Amazon S3 for 7 years. Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

o.t: Turn on S3 Object Lock with compliance retention mode for the S3 bucket. Set the retention period to expire after 7 years. Recopy all existing objects to bring the existing data into compliance.
o.w: Manually recopying every existing object to bring it under the new retention settings requires custom scripting and reprocessing of the entire existing dataset object by object, far more operational effort than a managed bulk operation.

o.t: Turn on the S3 Versioning feature for the S3 bucket. Configure S3 Lifecycle to delete the data after 7 years. Configure multi-factor authentication (MFA) delete for all S3 objects.
o.w: S3 Versioning with a lifecycle rule to delete data after 7 years does not prevent deletion or overwriting before that time, and MFA delete only adds a confirmation step; neither enforces the immutable, compliance-grade retention a legal requirement needs.

o.t: Turn on S3 Object Lock with compliance retention mode for the S3 bucket. Set the retention period to expire after 7 years. Use S3 Batch Operations to bring the existing data into compliance.
o.w: S3 Object Lock in compliance mode enforces an immutable retention period that even the account root user cannot override, meeting the legal retention requirement, and S3 Batch Operations can apply that retention setting to all existing objects in bulk without custom per-object scripting.

o.t: Turn on S3 Object Lock with governance retention mode for the S3 bucket. Set the retention period to expire after 7 years. Recopy all existing objects to bring the existing data into compliance.
o.w: Governance mode retention can be overridden by users granted special permissions (such as bypass-governance-retention), so it does not provide the same enforceable, non-overridable guarantee that a legal 7-year retention requirement calls for.

q: A company needs to migrate a MySQL database from its on-premises data center to AWS within 2 weeks. The database is 20 TB in size. The company wants to complete the migration with minimal downtime. Which solution will migrate the database MOST cost-effectively?

o.t: Order an AWS Snowball Edge Storage Optimized device. Use AWS Database Migration Service (AWS DMS) with AWS Schema Conversion Tool (AWS SCT) to migrate the database with replication of ongoing changes. Send the Snowball Edge device to AWS to finish the migration and continue the ongoing replication.
o.w: Snowball Edge Storage Optimized provides the large, cost-effective bulk capacity needed for a 20 TB database, and running DMS with SCT alongside it lets ongoing database changes keep replicating after the bulk data ships, minimizing cutover downtime once the device reaches AWS.

o.t: Order an AWS Snowball Edge Compute Optimized with GPU device. Use AWS Database Migration Service (AWS DMS) with AWS Schema Conversion Tool (AWS SCT) to migrate the database with ongoing changes. Send the Snowball device to AWS to finish the migration and continue the ongoing replication
o.w: The Compute Optimized with GPU variant is priced and designed for compute-intensive workloads such as machine learning or video processing, not bulk data transfer, so it costs more than the Storage Optimized device without providing any storage benefit here.

o.t: Order a 1 GB dedicated AWS Direct Connect connection to establish a connection with the data center. Use AWS Database Migration Service (AWS DMS) with AWS Schema Conversion Tool (AWS SCT) to migrate the database with replication of ongoing changes.
o.w: Provisioning a new dedicated 1 Gbps Direct Connect connection has setup lead time that can exceed the 2-week deadline and carries ongoing connection charges, making it both potentially too slow to establish and more expensive for a one-time 20 TB migration.

o.t: Order an AWS Snowmobile vehicle. Use AWS Database Migration Service (AWS DMS) with AWS Schema Conversion Tool (AWS SCT) to migrate the database with ongoing changes. Send the Snowmobile vehicle back to AWS to finish the migration and continue the ongoing replication.
o.w: An AWS Snowmobile is built for exabyte-scale migrations; using it for only 20 TB is a drastic cost and scale mismatch for this migration.

explain:
This is a cost-effective solution for shipping large amounts of data to AWS. Snowball Edge devices are designed for efficient data transfer, and they can handle the 20 TB database.

AWS DMS is a managed service for migrating databases to AWS, and AWS SCT can assist in converting the database schema. Using these tools in combination allows for a smooth migration process.

q: A company runs applications on Amazon EC2 instances in one AWS Region. The company wants to back up the EC2 instances to a second Region. The company also wants to provision EC2 resources in the second Region and manage the EC2 instances centrally from one AWS account. Which solution will meet these requirements MOST cost-effectively?

o.t: Deploy a similar number of EC2 instances in the second Region. Use AWS DataSync to transfer the data from the source Region to the second Region.
o.w: Manually deploying a matching EC2 fleet in the second Region and keeping data synced with DataSync means paying for and operating duplicate running infrastructure and custom sync jobs continuously, costing more than a managed backup copy that only stores backup data.

o.t: Create a backup plan by using AWS Backup. Configure cross-Region backup to the second Region for the EC2 instances.
o.w: AWS Backup centralizes scheduling and retention for EC2 backups and has a built-in cross-Region copy feature, letting the company back up and copy instances to the second Region from one central plan with no custom replication code or standing duplicate compute.

o.t: Create point-in-time Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) snapshots of the EC2 instances. Copy the snapshots to the second Region periodically.
o.w: Manually creating and periodically copying EBS snapshots without AWS Backup requires building your own scheduling, retention, and cross-Region copy automation, which is more operationally involved than a managed backup plan.

o.t: Create a disaster recovery (DR) plan that has a similar number of EC2 instances in the second Region. Configure data replication.
o.w: Running a parallel DR fleet of EC2 instances with ongoing data replication means paying for always-on compute capacity in the second Region, which is not the most cost-effective way to meet a backup-and-central-management requirement.

explain: AWS Backup is a centralized backup service that allows you to create backup plans for various AWS resources, including EC2 instances. With AWS Backup, you can configure cross-Region backups, meaning you can replicate backups from one AWS Region to another. This provides a cost-effective and centralized solution for backup.

q: A company wants to run a gaming application on Amazon EC2 instances that are part of an Auto Scaling group in the AWS Cloud. The application will transmit data by using UDP packets. The company wants to ensure that the application can scale out and in as traffic increases and decreases. What should a solutions architect do to meet these requirements?

o.t: Attach a Network Load Balancer to the Auto Scaling group.
o.w: Network Load Balancers operate at the transport layer and natively support UDP traffic, and an NLB can be attached to an Auto Scaling group so targets register and deregister automatically as the group scales, meeting both the UDP and elastic-scaling requirements.

o.t: Attach an Application Load Balancer to the Auto Scaling group.
o.w: Application Load Balancers operate at Layer 7 for HTTP/HTTPS and do not support UDP traffic at all, so an ALB cannot route this gaming application's UDP packets.

o.t: Deploy a NAT instance that is configured with port forwarding to the EC2 instances in the Auto Scaling group.
o.w: A single NAT instance is not part of an Auto Scaling group and represents a single point of failure and fixed-capacity bottleneck; it does not scale out and in with traffic as required.

o.t: Deploy an Amazon Route 53 record set with a weighted policy to route traffic appropriately.
o.w: Route 53 weighted routing distributes DNS resolutions across endpoints but does not perform the connection-level load balancing of UDP traffic to a dynamically scaling fleet that a load balancer provides.

explain: UDP is a connectionless protocol, and Network Load Balancers (NLB) support UDP, making them suitable for applications that use UDP for transmitting data.

q: An online learning company is migrating to the AWS Cloud. The company maintains its student records in a PostgreSQL database. The company needs a solution in which its data is available and online across multiple AWS Regions at all times. Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST amount of operational overhead?

o.t: Migrate the PostgreSQL database to an Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL DB instance. Create a read replica in another Region.
o.w: Creating a cross-Region read replica of the managed RDS for PostgreSQL instance keeps the data continuously available and online in a second Region, using RDS's built-in replication rather than any custom process, with minimal setup.

o.t: Migrate the PostgreSQL database to an Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL DB instance. Set up DB snapshots to be copied to another Region.
o.w: Periodic DB snapshot copies to another Region only provide point-in-time backups, not continuously available, up-to-date data in that Region; restoring from a snapshot after a need arises takes time and loses any changes made since the snapshot.

o.t: Migrate the PostgreSQL database to an Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL DB instance with the Multi-AZ feature turned on.
o.w: Multi-AZ protects against failure within a single Region (across AZs in that Region) but does not make the data available and online in a different AWS Region, which is the actual requirement.

o.t: Migrate the PostgreSQL database to a PostgreSQL cluster on Amazon EC2 instances.
o.w: Running a self-managed PostgreSQL cluster on EC2 requires manually setting up and maintaining replication, failover, and patching, far more operational overhead than RDS's built-in cross-Region read replicas.

explain: Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL allows you to create read replicas in different AWS Regions. This provides cross-Region availability and redundancy. Additionally, it allows you to offload read traffic from the primary database.

q: A company runs a public three-tier web application in a VPC. The application runs on Amazon EC2 instances across multiple Availability Zones. The EC2 instances that run in private subnets need to communicate with a license server over the internet. The company needs a managed solution that minimizes operational maintenance. Which solution meets these requirements?

o.t: Provision a NAT instance in a private subnet. Modify each private subnet's route table with a default route that points to the NAT instance.
o.w: A NAT instance requires the company to manage, patch, and scale an EC2 instance acting as the NAT device, and placing it in a private subnet would give it no direct path to the internet, which is both more operational burden and architecturally incorrect.

o.t: Provision a NAT gateway in a public subnet. Modify each private subnet's route table with a default route that points to the NAT gateway.
o.w: A NAT gateway is a fully managed AWS service with built-in high availability within its Availability Zone, and placing it in a public subnet (which routes to an internet gateway) while pointing the private subnets' route tables at it lets private instances reach the internet with minimal ongoing maintenance.

o.t: Provision a NAT instance in a public subnet. Modify each private subnet's route table with a default route that points to the NAT instance.
o.w: Using a NAT instance instead of a NAT gateway still requires the company to patch, scale, and monitor the underlying EC2 instance itself, which does not minimize operational maintenance the way the managed NAT gateway service does.

o.t: Provision a NAT gateway in a private subnet. Modify each private subnet's route table with a default route that points to the NAT gateway.
o.w: A NAT gateway placed in a private subnet would have no route to the internet, since private subnets lack a direct internet gateway route, so it could not actually provide outbound internet access to instances behind it.

explain:
NAT Gateway: A NAT gateway is a managed service provided by AWS that allows EC2 instances in private subnets to initiate outbound traffic to the internet while preventing unsolicited inbound traffic from reaching those instances. NAT gateways are fully managed, highly available, and require minimal maintenance.

Public Subnet: Placing the NAT gateway in a public subnet allows it to have access to the internet, fulfilling the requirement for private instances to communicate with a license server over the internet.

Default Route: Modifying each private subnet's route table with a default route that points to the NAT gateway ensures that traffic from private instances is directed through the NAT gateway for outbound communication.

q: A company wants to direct its users to a backup static error page if the company's primary website is unavailable. The primary website's DNS records are hosted in Amazon Route 53. The domain is pointing to an Application Load Balancer (ALB). The company needs a solution that minimizes changes and infrastructure overhead. Which solution will meet these requirements?

o.t: Update the Route 53 records to use a multivalue answer routing policy. Create a health check. Direct traffic to the website if the health check passes. Direct traffic to a static error page that is hosted in Amazon S3 if the health check does not pass.
o.w: Multivalue answer routing returns several IP answers for basic load distribution and health-check-based exclusion, but it is not purpose-built as a clean primary/backup failover model compared with Route 53's dedicated failover routing policy.

o.t: Set up a Route 53 active-active configuration with the ALB and an Amazon EC2 instance that hosts a static error page as endpoints. Configure Route 53 to send requests to the instance only if the health checks fail for the ALB.
o.w: Standing up and maintaining an EC2 instance just to host a simple static error page adds ongoing server management and cost that is unnecessary when the same page can be served directly from S3.

o.t: Set up a Route 53 active-passive failover configuration. Direct traffic to a static error page that is hosted in an Amazon S3 bucket when Route 53 health checks determine that the ALB endpoint is unhealthy.
o.w: Route 53 failover routing is purpose-built for exactly this primary/secondary pattern: a health check on the ALB determines whether traffic is routed to it, and traffic automatically shifts to the secondary S3-hosted static error page when the ALB is deemed unhealthy, needing no new infrastructure beyond the S3 bucket.

o.t: Update the Route 53 records to use a latency routing policy. Add a static error page that is hosted in an Amazon S3 bucket to the records so that the traffic is sent to the most responsive endpoints.
o.w: Latency-based routing sends users to whichever healthy endpoint responds fastest; it is designed for performance-based routing across multiple active Regions, not for an explicit active/backup failover scenario.

explain:
An active-passive failover configuration in Route 53 involves designating one endpoint (primary, in this case, the ALB) as active and another endpoint (S3 bucket hosting a static error page) as passive.
Route 53 health checks can be configured to monitor the health of the ALB endpoint. If the health checks determine that the ALB endpoint is unhealthy (i.e., the primary website is unavailable), Route 53 automatically directs traffic to the passive endpoint (S3 bucket with the static error page).

q: A company is developing a mobile gaming app in a single AWS Region. The app runs on multiple Amazon EC2 instances in an Auto Scaling group. The company stores the app data in Amazon DynamoDB. The app communicates by using TCP traffic and UDP traffic between the users and the servers. The application will be used globally. The company wants to ensure the lowest possible latency for all users. Which solution will meet these requirements?

o.t: Create an Amazon CloudFront content delivery network (CDN) endpoint. Create a Network Load Balancer (NLB) behind the endpoint and listening on the TCP and UDP ports. Update the Auto Scaling group to register instances on the NLB. Update CloudFront to use the NLB as the origin.
o.w: CloudFront is an HTTP/HTTPS content delivery network and cannot forward arbitrary TCP and UDP traffic to a Network Load Balancer the way Global Accelerator does, so it cannot carry this application's UDP traffic.

o.t: Create an Amazon CloudFront content delivery network (CDN) endpoint. Create an Application Load Balancer (ALB) behind the endpoint and listening on the TCP and UDP ports. Update the Auto Scaling group to register instances on the ALB. Update CloudFront to use the ALB as the origin.
o.w: CloudFront also cannot front an Application Load Balancer for UDP traffic, since both CloudFront and ALB operate at the HTTP/HTTPS layer with no support for UDP.

o.t: Use AWS Global Accelerator to create an accelerator. Create an Application Load Balancer (ALB) behind an accelerator endpoint that uses Global Accelerator integration and listening on the TCP and UDP ports. Update the Auto Scaling group to register instances on the ALB.
o.w: An Application Load Balancer operates at Layer 7 for HTTP/HTTPS and does not support UDP traffic, so it cannot handle this application's combined TCP/UDP communication.

o.t: Use AWS Global Accelerator to create an accelerator. Create a Network Load Balancer (NLB) behind an accelerator endpoint that uses Global Accelerator integration and listening on the TCP and UDP ports. Update the Auto Scaling group to register instances on the NLB.
o.w: AWS Global Accelerator uses static anycast IPs and the AWS global network to route users to the nearest healthy endpoint with low latency, and a Network Load Balancer behind it supports both TCP and UDP, correctly matching the application's mixed-protocol, globally distributed, latency-sensitive requirements.

q: A company uses AWS Organizations to manage multiple AWS accounts for different departments. The management account has an Amazon S3 bucket that contains project reports. The company wants to limit access to this S3 bucket to only users of accounts within the organization in AWS Organizations. Which solution meets these requirements with the LEAST amount of operational overhead?

o.t: Tag each user that needs access to the S3 bucket. Add the aws:PrincipalTag global condition key to the S3 bucket policy.
o.w: Tagging every individual user across the organization and maintaining aws:PrincipalTag conditions requires ongoing manual tagging and policy upkeep as users and accounts change, far more operational overhead than a single organization-wide condition key.

o.t: Use AWS CloudTrail to monitor the CreateAccount, InviteAccountToOrganization, LeaveOrganization, and RemoveAccountFromOrganization events. Update the S3 bucket policy accordingly.
o.w: Monitoring account membership events via CloudTrail and manually updating the bucket policy in response requires building custom automation or manual intervention every time accounts join or leave the organization, which is high operational overhead.

o.t: Add the aws PrincipalOrgID global condition key with a reference to the organization ID to the S3 bucket policy.
o.w: The aws:PrincipalOrgID condition key automatically scopes access to any principal belonging to the specified AWS Organization, so the bucket policy continues to correctly allow or deny access as accounts are added or removed, with no ongoing maintenance required.

o.t: Create an organizational unit (OU) for each department. Add the aws:PrincipalOrgPaths global condition key to the S3 bucket policy.
o.w: aws:PrincipalOrgPaths requires creating and maintaining organizational units and path-based conditions per department, adding structural overhead that isn't necessary when the goal is simply restricting access to any account in the whole organization.

explain:
aws:PrincipalOrgID – Simplifies specifying the Principal element in a resource-based policy. This global key provides an alternative to listing all the account IDs for all AWS accounts in an organization. Instead of listing all of the accounts that are members of an organization, you can specify the organization ID in the Condition element.
proposes adding the aws PrincipalOrgID global condition key with a reference to the organization ID to the S3 bucket policy. This would limit access to the S3 bucket to only users of accounts within the organization in AWS Organizations, as the aws PrincipalOrgID condition key can check if the request is coming from within the organization.

q: A company has an application that places hundreds of .csv files into an Amazon S3 bucket every hour. The files are 1 GB in size. Each time a file is uploaded, the company needs to convert the file to Apache Parquet format and place the output file into an S3 bucket. Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

o.t: Create an AWS Glue extract, transform, and load (ETL) job to convert the .csv files to Parquet format and place the output files into an S3 bucket. Create an AWS Lambda function for each S3 PUT event to invoke the ETL job.
o.w: An AWS Glue ETL job is a managed, serverless Spark-based service purpose-built for converting file formats like CSV to Parquet, and triggering it from a lightweight Lambda function on each S3 PUT event automates the conversion without managing any servers or clusters.

o.t: Create an AWS Glue table and an AWS Glue crawler for the S3 bucket where the application places the .csv files. Schedule an AWS Lambda function to periodically use Amazon Athena to query the AWS Glue table, convert the query results into Parquet format, and place the output files into an S3 bucket.
o.w: Periodically polling via a scheduled Lambda function that queries through Athena and reformats results introduces delay (it isn't triggered per file as it arrives) and added complexity compared with converting each uploaded file directly as it lands.

o.t: Create an AWS Lambda function to download the .csv files, convert the files to Parquet format, and place the output files in an S3 bucket. Invoke the Lambda function for each S3 PUT event.
o.w: Having Lambda itself download and convert each 1 GB CSV file risks hitting Lambda's execution time, memory, and temporary storage limits for files of that size, and it requires writing and maintaining custom conversion code instead of using a managed ETL service.

o.t: Create an Apache Spark job to read the .csv files, convert the files to Parquet format, and place the output files in an S3 bucket. Create an AWS Lambda function for each S3 PUT event to invoke the Spark job.
o.w: Standing up and operating a self-managed Apache Spark job outside of a managed service requires provisioning, managing, and scaling the Spark infrastructure yourself, more operational overhead than a Glue-managed ETL job.

explain:
AWS Glue ETL Job:

AWS Glue is a fully managed extract, transform, and load (ETL) service that can be used to convert data formats.
By creating an AWS Glue ETL job, you can offload the conversion process to a fully managed service, reducing operational overhead.
AWS Lambda for S3 PUT Events:
AWS Lambda can be configured to trigger on S3 PUT events. This ensures that the ETL job is invoked automatically each time a new .csv file is uploaded to the S3 bucket.
The Lambda function acts as a glue between the S3 events and the Glue ETL job.

q: A company hosts a marketing website in an on-premises data center. The website consists of static documents and runs on a single server. An administrator updates the website content infrequently and uses an SFTP client to upload new documents. The company decides to host its website on AWS and to use Amazon CloudFront. The company’s solutions architect creates a CloudFront distribution. The solutions architect must design the most cost-effective and resilient architecture for website hosting to serve as the CloudFront origin. Which solution will meet these requirements?

o.t: Create a public Amazon S3 bucket. Configure AWS Transfer for SFTP. Configure the S3 bucket for website hosting. Upload website content by using the SFTP client.
o.w: A public S3 bucket configured for website hosting is directly reachable over the internet, bypassing CloudFront entirely, and running AWS Transfer for SFTP just for infrequent uploads adds ongoing service cost for a need the AWS CLI already meets.

o.t: Create an AWS Auto Scaling group for Amazon EC2 instances. Use an Application Load Balancer. Upload website content by using an SFTP client.
o.w: Running an Auto Scaling group of EC2 instances behind an ALB to serve a handful of infrequently updated static documents is far more costly and operationally heavy than serving the same content from S3, which needs no server management at all.

o.t: Create a private Amazon S3 bucket. Use an S3 bucket policy to allow access from a CloudFront origin access identity (OAI). Upload website content by using the AWS CLI.
o.w: A private S3 bucket keeps content inaccessible directly from the internet, while a bucket policy allowing only the CloudFront origin access identity to fetch objects gives a secure, serverless, highly durable origin; the AWS CLI handles infrequent uploads with the permissions already available to the content administrator.

o.t: Create a virtual server by using Amazon Lightsail. Configure the web server in the Lightsail instance. Upload website content by using an SFTP client.
o.w: Amazon Lightsail still means running and maintaining a virtual server — patching, scaling, uptime — for what is just a small set of infrequently updated static documents, less cost-effective and less resilient than serving directly from S3.

explain: This option leverages Amazon S3 as the origin for CloudFront. By creating a private S3 bucket and using a bucket policy to allow access from a CloudFront origin access identity (OAI), you ensure that the content is served securely from S3 and that only CloudFront can access the bucket.

q: A company has Amazon EC2 instances that run nightly batch jobs to process data. The EC2 instances run in an Auto Scaling group that uses OnDemand billing. If a job fails on one instance, another instance will reprocess the job. The batch jobs run between 12:00 AM and 06:00 AM local time every day. Which solution will provide EC2 instances to meet these requirements MOST cost-effectively?

o.t: Create a new launch template for the Auto Scaling group. Set the instances to Spot Instances. Set a policy to scale out based on CPU usage.
o.w: Spot Instances offer substantial savings over On-Demand pricing, and because the batch jobs are fault-tolerant (a failed job is automatically reprocessed on another instance), occasional Spot interruptions are acceptable, while scaling out based on CPU usage still lets capacity grow to meet the nightly workload.

o.t: Create a new launch template for the Auto Scaling group. Increase the instance size. Set a policy to scale out based on CPU usage.
o.w: Simply increasing instance size while staying on On-Demand pricing raises the cost per hour without taking advantage of the batch jobs' fault tolerance to use cheaper, interruptible Spot capacity.

o.t: Purchase a 1-year Reserved Instance for the specific instance type and operating system of the instances in the Auto Scaling group that the batch job uses.
o.w: A 1-year Reserved Instance commits to paying for capacity every hour of every day, even though the batch jobs run only during a roughly 6-hour nightly window, so the company would pay for far more idle capacity than it uses.

o.t: Purchase a 1-year Savings Plan for Amazon EC2 that covers the instance family of the Auto Scaling group that the batch job uses.
o.w: A Savings Plan likewise commits to a consistent hourly spend across the whole day for an instance family, which doesn't match a workload that only needs compute capacity for a few hours each night, wasting the commitment during idle hours.

explain:
Spot Instances: Spot Instances allow you to bid for unused EC2 capacity at a potentially lower cost than On-Demand pricing. This can result in significant cost savings for batch jobs that are fault-tolerant and can be interrupted or retried.

Scaling Policy: Setting a policy to scale out based on CPU usage ensures that additional Spot Instances are launched when the demand for processing power increases during batch job execution. This helps in handling varying workloads efficiently.

q: A company is reviewing a recent migration of a three-tier application to a VPC. The security team discovers that the principle of least privilege is not being applied to Amazon EC2 security group ingress and egress rules between the application tiers. What should a solutions architect do to correct this issue?

o.t: Create security group rules using the security group ID as the source or destination.
o.w: Referencing security group IDs as the source or destination in ingress/egress rules automatically scopes access to exactly the instances that belong to those groups, regardless of how many instances exist or their individual IPs, enforcing least privilege precisely between application tiers.

o.t: Create security group rules using the instance ID as the source or destination.
o.w: Security group rules cannot reference individual instance IDs as a source or destination; rules are defined using IP ranges, prefix lists, or other security group IDs, so this mechanism does not exist as described.

o.t: Create security group rules using the VPC CIDR blocks as the source or destination.
o.w: Using the entire VPC CIDR block as the source or destination opens access to every resource in the VPC, not just the specific tier that should be allowed to communicate, which works against least privilege rather than correcting it.

o.t: Create security group rules using the subnet CIDR blocks as the source or destination.
o.w: Using subnet CIDR blocks still grants access to every resource in that subnet rather than only the specific instances belonging to the correct application tier, so it remains broader than least privilege requires.

explain: Using security group IDs allows for dynamic and flexible configuration. Referencing security groups directly in rules ensures that instances associated with those security groups, regardless of their individual IDs, are included. This approach aligns with the principle of least privilege and simplifies rule management.

q: A company is developing a microservices application that will provide a search catalog for customers. The company must use REST APIs to present the frontend of the application to users. The REST APIs must access the backend services that the company hosts in containers in private VPC subnets. Which solution will meet these requirements?

o.t: Design a REST API by using Amazon API Gateway. Host the application in Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) in a private subnet. Create a private VPC link for API Gateway to access Amazon ECS.
o.w: A REST API in API Gateway matches the stated requirement for REST APIs, and a private VPC Link lets API Gateway securely and directly reach backend ECS services in private VPC subnets without exposing them publicly or needing a NAT/internet path.

o.t: Design a WebSocket API by using Amazon API Gateway. Host the application in Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) in a private subnet. Create a security group for API Gateway to access Amazon ECS.
o.w: A WebSocket API is designed for persistent, bidirectional connections such as chat or live updates, not for a standard REST API as explicitly required by the question.

o.t: Design a REST API by using Amazon API Gateway. Host the application in Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) in a private subnet. Create a security group for API Gateway to access Amazon ECS.
o.w: A security group alone provides no network-level connectivity path from API Gateway into a private VPC subnet; without a VPC Link (or VPC endpoint), API Gateway has no private network route to reach resources in private subnets.

o.t: Design a WebSocket API by using Amazon API Gateway. Host the application in Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) in a private subnet. Create a private VPC link for API Gateway to access Amazon ECS.
o.w: This combines a WebSocket API — the wrong API type for the stated REST requirement — with a correctly used VPC Link, so it still fails the explicit requirement that the frontend be built using REST APIs.

q: A company wants to migrate a Windows-based application from on premises to the AWS Cloud. The application has three tiers: an application tier, a business tier, and a database tier with Microsoft SQL Server. The company wants to use specific features of SQL Server such as native backups and Data Quality Services. The company also needs to share files for processing between the tiers. How should a solutions architect design the architecture to meet these requirements?

o.t: Host all three tiers on Amazon EC2 instances. Use Amazon FSx for Windows File Server for file sharing between the tiers.
o.w: Amazon FSx for Windows File Server is a fully managed Windows-native file system reachable over SMB, giving the Windows-based tiers a native shared file system for inter-tier processing, while hosting all tiers on EC2 preserves the full engine-level control that SQL Server's native backups and Data Quality Services require.

o.t: Host all three tiers on Amazon EC2 instances. Use Amazon FSx File Gateway for file sharing between the tiers.
o.w: FSx File Gateway is meant to cache on-premises access to an FSx file system for hybrid workloads; since all tiers already run in AWS, it adds an unnecessary extra component rather than providing the direct inter-tier file sharing that's needed.

o.t: Host the application tier and the business tier on Amazon EC2 instances. Host the database tier on Amazon RDS. Use Amazon Elastic File System (Amazon EFS) for file sharing between the tiers.
o.w: Moving the database tier to Amazon RDS means giving up the native SQL Server features such as native backups and Data Quality Services, since RDS is a managed service that doesn't expose the full OS/engine-level access those features require.

o.t: Host the application tier and the business tier on Amazon EC2 instances. Host the database tier on Amazon RDS. Use a Provisioned IOPS SSD (io2) Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) volume for file sharing between the tiers.
o.w: An EBS volume can normally be attached to only one instance at a time, so it cannot serve as a shared file system for processing between separate application, business, and database tiers, and moving the database to RDS again loses the required native SQL Server features.

explain:
hosting all three tiers on Amazon EC2 instances allows you to have flexibility and control over the entire application architecture. To address the file-sharing requirement between the tiers, you can use Amazon FSx for Windows File Server.

Amazon FSx for Windows File Server is a fully managed Windows file system that is accessible from Windows-based instances over the Server Message Block (SMB) protocol. It supports the specific features of Windows File Server, including features like native backups and access to Windows-specific services.

q: A company has launched an Amazon RDS for MySQL DB instance. Most of the connections to the database come from serverless applications. Application traffic to the database changes significantly at random intervals. At times of high demand, users report that their applications experience database connection rejection errors. Which solution will resolve this issue with the LEAST operational overhead?

o.t: Migrate the DB instance to a different instance class that has higher I/O capacity. Configure the users’ applications to use the new DB instance.
o.w: Changing to a higher-I/O instance class addresses throughput, not the number of concurrent connections; serverless applications opening many short-lived connections cause connection exhaustion regardless of the instance's I/O capacity.

o.t: Deploy Amazon ElastiCache for Memcached between the users’ applications and the DB instance.
o.w: ElastiCache for Memcached is a data cache, not a connection pooler or proxy for the database protocol; it does not multiplex or manage the underlying database connections that are being rejected.

o.t: Create a proxy in RDS Proxy. Configure the users’ applications to use the DB instance through RDS Proxy.
o.w: RDS Proxy sits between the many ephemeral serverless application connections and the database, pooling and reusing a smaller number of actual database connections, which directly resolves connection exhaustion and rejection errors with no application code changes.

o.t: Configure Multi-AZ for the DB instance. Configure the users’ applications to switch between the DB instances.
o.w: Multi-AZ provides failover protection for availability, not connection pooling; it does not increase the number of connections the database can accept or reduce connection churn from serverless clients.

explain: RDS Proxy is a fully managed, highly available database proxy for Amazon RDS that makes applications more scalable, more resilient to database failures, and more secure. It automatically routes database traffic to the appropriate DB instance, handling connection pooling and failover.

q: A hospital needs to store patient records in an Amazon S3 bucket. The hospital’s compliance team must ensure that all protected health information (PHI) is encrypted in transit and at rest. The compliance team must administer the encryption key for data at rest. Which solution will meet these requirements?

o.t: Use the aws:SecureTransport condition on S3 bucket policies to allow only encrypted connections over HTTPS (TLS). Use Amazon Macie to protect the sensitive data that is stored in Amazon S3. Assign the compliance team to manage Macie.
o.w: Amazon Macie discovers and classifies sensitive data; it is not an encryption mechanism and gives the compliance team no way to administer an encryption key, so it does not satisfy the key-administration requirement at all.

o.t: Use the aws:SecureTransport condition on S3 bucket policies to allow only encrypted connections over HTTPS (TLS). Configure default encryption for each S3 bucket to use server-side encryption with S3 managed encryption keys (SSE-S3). Assign the compliance team to manage the SSE-S3 keys.
o.w: With SSE-S3, AWS fully owns and manages the encryption keys, so the compliance team has no ability to administer or control those keys, which fails the explicit requirement that the compliance team administer the key.

o.t: Use the aws:SecureTransport condition on S3 bucket policies to allow only encrypted connections over HTTPS (TLS). Configure default encryption for each S3 bucket to use server-side encryption with AWS KMS keys (SSE-KMS). Assign the compliance team to manage the KMS keys.
o.w: The aws:SecureTransport condition enforces encryption in transit, and SSE-KMS encrypts data at rest using a customer-managed KMS key whose key policy and administration can be assigned to the compliance team, directly meeting both the in-transit and admin-controlled at-rest encryption requirements.

o.t: Create a public SSL/TLS certificate in AWS Certificate Manager (ACM). Associate the certificate with Amazon S3. Configure default encryption for each S3 bucket to use server-side encryption with AWS KMS keys (SSE-KMS). Assign the compliance team to manage the KMS keys.
o.w: A public SSL/TLS certificate in ACM is used to secure custom domains or applications, such as behind CloudFront or a load balancer; it is not how S3 enforces transport encryption at the bucket level, so attaching an ACM certificate this way does not reflect how S3 actually works.

explain: it allows the compliance team to manage the KMS keys used for server-side encryption, thereby providing the necessary control over the encryption keys. Additionally, the use of the "aws:SecureTransport" condition on the bucket policy ensures that all connections to the S3 bucket are encrypted in transit.

q: A company uses locally attached storage to run a latency-sensitive application on premises. The company is using a lift and shift method to move the application to the AWS Cloud. The company does not want to change the application architecture. Which solution will meet these requirements MOST cost-effectively?

o.t: Host the application on an Amazon EC2 instance. Use an Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) GP3 volume to run the application.
o.w: Hosting the application on EC2 with a gp3 EBS volume replicates the on-premises locally attached block-storage model with no architecture change, while gp3 provides low-latency block storage with configurable IOPS and throughput at a lower cost than other provisioned-performance volume types.

o.t: Configure an Auto Scaling group with an Amazon EC2 instance. Use an Amazon FSx for Lustre file system to run the application.
o.w: FSx for Lustre is a distributed, shared parallel file system meant for HPC-style workloads accessed by many compute nodes at once; adopting it would restructure the application's storage access model, which the company explicitly wants to avoid, and it costs more than a simple attached EBS volume.

o.t: Host the application on an Amazon EC2 instance. Use an Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) GP2 volume to run the application.
o.w: gp2 volumes tie performance to the size of the volume and generally offer a less favorable price-to-performance ratio than gp3 for the same performance level, making gp3 the more cost-effective choice between the two.

o.t: Configure an Auto Scaling group with an Amazon EC2 instance. Use an Amazon FSx for OpenZFS file system to run the application.
o.w: FSx for OpenZFS is a shared network file system service that, like Lustre, changes the storage access pattern from simple locally attached block storage to a networked file protocol, again requiring architecture changes the company wants to avoid.

explain: Amazon EC2 Instance with GP3 Volume (Option D): Amazon EBS GP3 volumes are designed to provide cost savings compared to GP2 volumes while still offering good performance for a broad range of workloads. GP3 volumes allow you to provision the IOPS (input/output operations per second) and throughput that your application needs, giving you flexibility and cost-effectiveness.

q: A company has multiple VPCs across AWS Regions to support and run workloads that are isolated from workloads in other Regions. Because of a recent application launch requirement, the company’s VPCs must communicate with all other VPCs across all Regions. Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST amount of administrative effort?

o.t: Use AWS Direct Connect gateways across all Regions to connect VPCs across regions and manage VPC communications.
o.w: Direct Connect gateways connect on-premises networks to VPCs over Direct Connect; they are not the mechanism AWS provides for interconnecting VPCs with each other, so they don't address this VPC-to-VPC requirement.

o.t: Use AWS PrivateLink across all Regions to connect VPCs across Regions and manage VPC communications
o.w: AWS PrivateLink is designed to privately expose a specific service endpoint to consumers, not to provide general full-mesh network connectivity between many VPCs across Regions, so it would need far more setup per connection than a hub-and-spoke model.

o.t: Use VPC peering to manage VPC communication in a single Region. Use VPC peering across Regions to manage VPC communications.
o.w: Using VPC peering for every VPC pair, both within and across Regions, requires manually creating and maintaining a separate peering connection and route table entries for every pair, which becomes administratively complex as the number of VPCs and Regions grows.

o.t: Use AWS Transit Gateway to manage VPC communication in a single Region and Transit Gateway peering across Regions to manage VPC communications.
o.w: AWS Transit Gateway provides hub-and-spoke connectivity within a Region, and Transit Gateway peering extends that hub-and-spoke model across Regions, so every VPC needs only one attachment to its local Transit Gateway rather than a full mesh of individual peering connections, minimizing ongoing administrative effort.

explain:
AWS Transit Gateway is designed for simplifying the connectivity between multiple VPCs and on-premises networks. It allows for hub-and-spoke connectivity patterns, making it easier to manage communication across multiple VPCs.
By using AWS Transit Gateway in a single Region to connect VPCs and enabling Transit Gateway peering across Regions, you can efficiently manage communication between VPCs in different Regions with centralized control and minimal administrative effort.

q: A media company hosts its website on AWS. The website application’s architecture includes a fleet of Amazon EC2 instances behind an Application Load Balancer (ALB) and a database that is hosted on Amazon Aurora. The company’s cybersecurity team reports that the application is vulnerable to SQL injection. How should the company resolve this issue?

o.t: Set up Amazon Inspector to block all SQL injection attempts automatically.
o.w: Amazon Inspector scans for software vulnerabilities and network exposure on EC2, container, and Lambda workloads; it does not inspect or block live HTTP requests for SQL injection patterns.

o.t: Subscribe to AWS Shield Advanced to block all SQL injection attempts automatically.
o.w: AWS Shield Advanced protects against DDoS attacks; it has no capability to inspect HTTP request content for SQL injection payloads, which is a web-application-layer exploit, not a volumetric or protocol attack.

o.t: Use AWS WAF in front of the ALB. Associate the appropriate web ACLs with AWS WAF.
o.w: AWS WAF can be attached to the ALB with managed or custom rules, including SQL injection rule sets, in a web ACL, inspecting and blocking malicious HTTP requests before they ever reach the application, directly addressing the SQL injection vulnerability.

o.t: Create an ALB listener rule to reply to SQL injections with a fixed response.
o.w: An ALB listener rule can only route traffic or return fixed responses based on basic request attributes; it has no request-content inspection engine capable of detecting or blocking SQL injection payloads.

explain:
AWS WAF (Web Application Firewall): AWS WAF is designed to protect web applications from common web exploits, including SQL injection. It allows you to create web access control lists (web ACLs) to define rules that filter and monitor HTTP traffic to your application.

Associating Web ACLs with AWS WAF: By using AWS WAF in front of the ALB, you can define rules to block or allow web requests based on conditions that you specify. This includes protection against SQL injection attempts. AWS WAF provides a range of conditions and rulesets that you can use to mitigate common security threats.

q: A company designed a stateless two-tier application that uses Amazon EC2 in a single Availability Zone and an Amazon RDS Multi-AZ DB instance. New company management wants to ensure the application is highly available. What should a solutions architect do to meet this requirement?

o.t: Configure the application to take snapshots of the EC2 instances and send them to a different AWS Region
o.w: Taking EC2 snapshots and sending them to another Region addresses backup and DR for a different Region, not the immediate need to make the existing single-AZ application tier highly available within its current setup.

o.t: Configure the application to use Multi-AZ EC2 Auto Scaling and create an Application Load Balancer
o.w: Configuring the EC2 Auto Scaling group to span multiple Availability Zones and placing an Application Load Balancer in front of it removes the application tier's single-AZ single point of failure, while the database tier is already Multi-AZ, together giving the stateless two-tier app full high availability.

o.t: Configure Amazon Route 53 rules to handle incoming requests and create a Multi-AZ Application Load Balancer
o.w: Route 53 rules alone do not create multi-AZ compute redundancy, and an ALB is inherently spread across the AZs you select regardless of being called "Multi-AZ" — but without a Multi-AZ Auto Scaling group behind it, the compute tier still lacks redundant instances across AZs.

o.t: Configure the application to use Amazon Route 53 latency-based routing to feed requests to the application
o.w: Route 53 latency-based routing directs users to the lowest-latency endpoint among multiple deployments; it does nothing to add Availability Zone redundancy to a single-AZ EC2 deployment within one Region.

q: A company is creating a new application that will store a large amount of data. The data will be analyzed hourly and will be modified by several Amazon EC2 Linux instances that are deployed across multiple Availability Zones. The needed amount of storage space will continue to grow for the next 6 months. Which storage solution should a solutions architect recommend to meet these requirements?

o.t: Store the data in an Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) Provisioned IOPS volume shared between the application instances.
o.w: A Provisioned IOPS EBS volume can normally be attached to only one instance at a time and is confined to a single Availability Zone, so it cannot be directly shared and modified concurrently by instances spread across multiple Availability Zones.

o.t: Store the data in an Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) volume. Mount the EBS volume on the application instances.
o.w: A standard EBS volume has the same single-attachment, single-AZ limitation, so it cannot serve as shared, concurrently writable storage for instances in multiple Availability Zones.

o.t: Store the data in an Amazon Elastic File System (Amazon EFS) file system. Mount the file system on the application instances.
o.w: Amazon EFS is a regional, elastic NFS file system that multiple EC2 Linux instances across different Availability Zones can mount and modify concurrently, and its storage automatically grows (and shrinks) with the data, directly matching the shared-access and continual-growth requirements.

o.t: Store the data in Amazon S3 Glacier. Update the S3 Glacier vault policy to allow access to the application instances.
o.w: S3 Glacier is designed for infrequently accessed archival data with retrieval delays ranging from minutes to hours; it is not suited for data that must be actively modified hourly by multiple compute instances.

explain: Amazon EFS is a scalable and fully managed file storage service that can be mounted on multiple Amazon EC2 instances simultaneously. It provides a shared file system that can be accessed concurrently from different instances.Amazon EFS can automatically scale its file system capacity to accommodate growing data sets. It can handle a large amount of data and is designed to grow and shrink as needed.

q: An ecommerce company has noticed performance degradation of its Amazon RDS based web application. The performance degradation is attributed to an increase in the number of read-only SQL queries triggered by business analysts. A solutions architect needs to solve the problem with minimal changes to the existing web application. What should the solutions architect recommend?

o.t: Load the data into Amazon ElastiCache and have the business analysts run their queries.
o.w: Loading all the data into ElastiCache requires building and maintaining a separate caching and loading pipeline, and it doesn't naturally support ad hoc, evolving analytical SQL the way a database read replica does.

o.t: Copy the data into an Amazon Redshift cluster and have the business analysts run their queries.
o.w: Copying data into a new Amazon Redshift cluster means standing up and managing an entirely new data warehouse and ETL process, a bigger architectural change than the "minimal changes" requirement calls for.

o.t: Create a read replica of the primary database and have the business analysts run their queries.
o.w: Creating a read replica lets the business analysts' read-only queries run against a separate database copy instead of the primary, offloading the extra query load with minimal application changes since the analysts simply point their queries at the replica's endpoint.

o.t: Export the data to Amazon DynamoDB and have the business analysts run their queries.
o.w: Exporting data to DynamoDB changes the data model from relational to NoSQL, which would likely break the analysts' existing SQL-based queries and represents a much larger change than minimal.

explain:
Creating a read replica is a common approach to offload read-only queries from the primary database, improving overall performance.
A read replica is an asynchronous copy of the primary database that allows for read-only operations.

Read replicas can be transparently used by the web application without requiring changes to the application logic.
Business analysts can direct their read-only queries to the read replica, reducing the load on the primary database.

q: A company is planning to store data on Amazon RDS DB instances. The company must encrypt the data at rest. What should a solutions architect do to meet this requirement?

o.t: Generate a certificate in AWS Certificate Manager (ACM). Enable SSL/TLS on the DB instances by using the certificate.
o.w: An ACM certificate with SSL/TLS secures data in transit (connections to the database), not data at rest on disk, so it does not meet the requirement to encrypt data at rest.

o.t: Generate a certificate in AWS Identity and Access Management (IAM). Enable SSL/TLS on the DB instances by using the certificate. Topic 1
o.w: IAM does not issue SSL/TLS certificates for encrypting database connections, and even if it did, that would again only address data in transit, not encryption of the data at rest.

o.t: Create a key in AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS). Enable encryption for the DB instances.
o.w: Creating a KMS key and enabling encryption on the RDS DB instance uses RDS's native at-rest encryption feature, which transparently encrypts the underlying storage, automated backups, and snapshots using the specified KMS key.

o.t: Create an encryption key. Store the key in AWS Secrets Manager. Use the key to encrypt the DB instances.
o.w: RDS at-rest encryption is configured through direct KMS key integration at the instance level, not by storing a custom-created key in AWS Secrets Manager and using it to encrypt the instance, which is not how RDS encryption at rest actually works.

explain:
By creating a key in AWS KMS and enabling encryption for the RDS DB instances, you ensure that the data at rest is encrypted using the specified key.

AWS RDS supports encryption at rest, and you can use AWS KMS to manage the encryption keys. When you enable encryption for an RDS DB instance, you can specify a KMS key to use for encryption.

q: A company runs analytics software on Amazon EC2 instances. The software accepts job requests from users to process data that has been uploaded to Amazon S3. Users report that some submitted data is not being processed Amazon CloudWatch reveals that the EC2 instances have a consistent CPU utilization at or near 100%. The company wants to improve system performance and scale the system based on user load. What should a solutions architect do to meet these requirements?

o.t: Create a copy of the instance. Place all instances behind an Application Load Balancer.
o.w: Simply duplicating the instance and adding an ALB still ties processing capacity to a fixed or manually managed number of instances; it does not introduce scaling based on queue backlog or relieve the CPU bottleneck as load varies.

o.t: Stop the EC2 instances. Modify the instance type to one with a more powerful CPU and more memory. Restart the instances.
o.w: Upgrading the instance type provides a one-time, static capacity bump but does not scale automatically with fluctuating job submission volume, so CPU utilization could again reach 100% as load grows.

o.t: Create an S3 VPC endpoint for Amazon S3. Update the software to reference the endpoint.
o.w: An S3 VPC endpoint improves the network path to S3; it has no effect on CPU-bound processing capacity or on scaling the number of workers to match job submission load.

o.t: Route incoming requests to Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS). Configure an EC2 Auto Scaling group based on queue size. Update the software to read from the queue.
o.w: Routing job requests through SQS decouples submission from processing, and configuring an Auto Scaling group to scale based on queue depth lets compute capacity grow and shrink automatically to match the actual backlog, directly resolving the CPU saturation and enabling load-based scaling.

explain: This option addresses the issue by offloading incoming requests to an SQS queue, allowing for decoupling of processing and scaling based on queue size. This helps improve system performance and allows for scaling based on user load.

q: A weather forecasting company needs to process hundreds of gigabytes of data with sub-millisecond latency. The company has a high performance computing (HPC) environment in its data center and wants to expand its forecasting capabilities. A solutions architect must identify a highly available cloud storage solution that can handle large amounts of sustained throughput. Files that are stored in the solution should be accessible to thousands of compute instances that will simultaneously access and process the entire dataset. What should the solutions architect do to meet these requirements?

o.t: Use Amazon FSx for Lustre scratch file systems.
o.w: Scratch file systems in FSx for Lustre are meant for temporary, high-performance processing where data doesn't need to persist independently of the file system, and they lack the data replication that persistent file systems provide, so they don't meet a requirement for durable, highly available storage.

o.t: Use Amazon Elastic File System (Amazon EFS) with Bursting Throughput mode.
o.w: EFS Bursting Throughput scales based on the size of the file system and accumulated burst credits, which doesn't reliably sustain the sub-millisecond, massively parallel, sustained high throughput that thousands of simultaneous HPC instances accessing a full dataset require.

o.t: Use Amazon Elastic File System (Amazon EFS) with Provisioned Throughput mode.
o.w: Even EFS Provisioned Throughput, while allowing a fixed throughput level independent of storage size, is still built on general-purpose NFS semantics and doesn't match the sub-millisecond latency and massively parallel access patterns a Lustre-based HPC file system is purpose-built for.

o.t: Use Amazon FSx for Lustre persistent file systems.
o.w: FSx for Lustre persistent file systems provide a highly available, durable, high-throughput parallel file system purpose-built for HPC workloads, letting thousands of compute instances simultaneously access and process the same dataset at the latency and sustained throughput the forecasting workload needs.

explain: Persistent file systems in FSx for Lustre are designed for longer-term storage needs. They provide a durable and highly available solution for your data. This is important for the weather forecasting company's requirement to handle large amounts of sustained throughput.

q: A company wants to give a customer the ability to use on-premises Microsoft Active Directory to download files that are stored in Amazon S3. The customer’s application uses an SFTP client to download the files. Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead and no changes to the customer’s application?

o.t: Set up AWS Transfer Family with SFTP for Amazon S3. Configure integrated Active Directory authentication.
o.w: AWS Transfer Family provides a fully managed SFTP endpoint in front of S3 and supports integrating authentication directly with on-premises Active Directory, so the customer's existing SFTP client keeps working unchanged while users authenticate with their familiar AD credentials.

o.t: Set up AWS Database Migration Service (AWS DMS) to synchronize the on-premises client with Amazon S3. Configure integrated Active Directory authentication.
o.w: AWS DMS is designed for migrating and replicating database workloads, not for exposing an SFTP interface backed by file storage, so it doesn't provide the SFTP access pattern or AD-integrated file authentication the customer's application needs.

o.t: Set up AWS DataSync to synchronize between the on-premises location and the S3 location by using AWS IAM Identity Center (AWS Single Sign-On).
o.w: AWS DataSync synchronizes files between storage systems but does not expose an SFTP server interface for client applications, and it integrates with AWS IAM Identity Center rather than on-premises Active Directory, so the existing SFTP client would not be able to connect without changes.

o.t: Set up a Windows Amazon EC2 instance with SFTP to connect the on-premises client with Amazon S3. Integrate AWS Identity and Access Management (IAM).
o.w: Standing up and operating a custom Windows EC2 instance running SFTP software requires patching, scaling, and maintaining a server yourself, considerably more operational overhead than a managed AWS Transfer Family endpoint, even though IAM integration is possible.

explain:
AWS Transfer Family with SFTP for Amazon S3: AWS Transfer Family is a fully managed service that allows you to set up an SFTP (Secure File Transfer Protocol) service for Amazon S3. It enables you to transfer files directly to and from Amazon S3 using the SFTP protocol.

Integrated Active Directory Authentication: AWS Transfer Family allows you to configure authentication with Microsoft Active Directory. By integrating with Active Directory, you can provide users with seamless access to S3 resources using their existing credentials without modifying their applications.

q: A company is running a custom application on Amazon EC2 On-Demand Instances. The application has frontend nodes that need to run 24 hours a day, 7 days a week and backend nodes that need to run only for a short time based on workload. The number of backend nodes varies during the day. The company needs to scale out and scale in more instances based on workload. Which solution will meet these requirements MOST cost-effectively?

o.t: Use Reserved Instances for the frontend nodes. Use AWS Fargate for the backend nodes.
o.w: AWS Fargate for the backend nodes removes EC2 management but is generally priced at a premium compared with EC2 Spot pricing, so it does not minimize cost for a backend workload that can tolerate interruption as well as using Spot Instances directly would.

o.t: Use Spot Instances for the frontend nodes. Use Reserved Instances for the backend nodes.
o.w: Using Spot Instances for the always-on frontend nodes risks interruption of a tier required to run 24/7, which could cause availability problems, while Reserved Instances for the variable-count backend commit to paying for fixed capacity that doesn't match a workload whose size changes throughout the day.

o.t: Use Spot Instances for the frontend nodes. Use AWS Fargate for the backend nodes.
o.w: Spot Instances for the 24/7 frontend tier risk interruption of nodes that must always be running, undermining continuous availability, and while Fargate for the backend is workable, it is typically costlier than Spot EC2 for this variable, interruption-tolerant workload.

o.t: Use Reserved Instances for the frontend nodes. Use Spot Instances for the backend nodes.
o.w: Reserved Instances give the steep discount appropriate for frontend nodes that run continuously, while Spot Instances let the backend take advantage of spare capacity at a much lower cost for a workload that varies in size and can tolerate interruption, matching each tier's purchasing model to its actual usage pattern.

explain:
Reserved Instances (RIs) for Frontend Nodes: Since the frontend nodes need to run 24/7, Reserved Instances provide a significant cost savings compared to On-Demand pricing. RIs are a commitment to a consistent usage pattern, making them suitable for instances that need to run continuously.

Spot Instances for Backend Nodes: Spot Instances are a cost-effective option for workloads that can be interrupted or are flexible regarding availability. As the number of backend nodes varies during the day, using Spot Instances allows you to take advantage of spare capacity at a lower cost. Spot Instances are suitable for short-lived, scalable, and flexible workloads.
